name: Donagha

attributes.attribute: was a lazy married man from the southwest of Ireland
wasted a wish making his wood walk home by itself
was sent far away when Donagha wished it
was the cabin destination of Varia in County Kerry
was Donaghadee near Belfast in County Down

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Donagha is an Irish folkloric character. He lived in the far southwest of Ireland with his wife Varia. Donagha was lazy. Varia was quarrelsome. The couple fought constantly and viciously. The fairy folk granted them two wishes. Donagha was so lazy he wasted one wish. He asked that his load of wood walk home by itself. The wood grew legs and did so. When Donagha reached home with his strange companion, Varia scolded him. She said he wasted a good wish. Donagha then wished her far away. Her cabin flew off at once to Teach na Vauria in County Kerry. Donagha himself flew to Teach an Donagha. This was Donaghadee, near Belfast, in County Down, at the other end of the island.

okr.objective: Record Donagha as the lazy Irish folk character who wasted a fairy wish.
key_results: Donagha was a lazy man whose wife Varia constantly carped at him.
The fairy folk granted the couple two wishes.
He wasted one wish by making his load of wood walk home by itself.
His second wish carried Varia to County Kerry and him to Donaghadee in County Down.
